https://metro.co.uk/2026/08/22/two-peopl.text: Two men have died and three people were arrested after the fatal crash in Surrey (Picture: Google) Two young men have died after three Seat Leons crashed on an A road in Surrey overnight. The UK’s roads saw several tragedies last night after fatal crashes claimed lives across the country. In Surrey, the alarm was raised after a multi-vehicle collision on Epsom Road in East Clandon shortly after 11pm. The emergency services found that a white, black and grey Seat Leon had smashed on the A246 near Clandon Wood Nature Reserve outside Guildford. The driver of the white Seat, a man in his late teens, and his passenger, a man aged in his early 20s, succumbed to their injuries at the scene. Their next of kin have been informed, Surrey Police confirmed. Now a 22-year-old man from Woking, a 21-year-old woman and a 19-year-old man, both from Guildford, have been arrested. They remain in police custody on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. Epsom Road A246 remains closed while an investigation is being carried out. Surrey Police asked anyone who was in the area between 10.50pm and 11pm yesterday or has dashcam footage to get in touch. The collision happened shortly before several people died in a crash on the A66 in Cleveland, North Yorkshire, following a police pursuit, marking a dark night for emergency services up and down the country. The police watchdog, IOPC, has launched an investigation into the incident as a pursuit was involved. In Kent, a stretch of the M20 was closed between junction J4 and J6 at Aylesford following another overnight crash. The motorway has been shut into the afternoon after a serious crash at about 3.20am today. Kent Police confirmed that a teenage girl died after being struck by vehicles, including a Ford Transit van and a Vauxhall Corsa. She was confirmed dead at the scene. Sarkis FUGE And Tadeusz Kantor: The Return of Odysseus September 5–October 11, 2026 Maxim Gorki Theater Am Festungsgraben 2 Berlin 10117 Germany gorki.de Instagram / Facebook / YouTube On September 4, we are opening the first season of the Maxim Gorki Theater ’ s new artistic direction with FUGE . The artist we have invited to begin this new chapter with us is Sarkis . Born in Istanbul in 1938 into an Armenian family and based in Paris since 1964, Sarkis has spent more than six decades moving between contemporary art, music, architecture, memory and theatre. He has participated in documenta and exhibited in major institutions internationally. As a guest of the DAAD Artists-in-Berlin Programme in 1978, he began Kriegsschatz—an ever-growing body of work in which objects, images and memories migrate across histories. FUGE is both the title and the principle of this new constellation. Like the independent voices of a musical fugue, the artists, works and histories within it remain distinct while transforming one another. Sarkis calls his works mises-en-scène: acts of invitation. Throughout his oeuvre, Sarkis has brought objects marked by displacement, conflict and memory into new relationships with colour, light, sound and architecture. His works are not closed compositions, but living constellations: they carry their histories with them while remaining open to transformation and to the presence of others. Within FUGE , Sarkis posthumously invites Tadeusz Kantor (1915–1990), Poland ’ s theatre revolutionary with the historical stage that travelled with him and his ensemble wherever they performed—an inseparable member of the ensemble and a mobile territory on which their theatre could emerge. The project extends Gorki ’ s collaboration with Kraków ’ s Cricoteka, the Centre for the Documentation of the Art of Tadeusz Kantor. At its heart is an entirely new work, conceived by Sarkis and brought to life in the Gorki workshops: an ancient skull becomes a mirror, carrying the trace of Sarkis ’ s own face. Rain falls onto its seven parts in the seven colors of the rainbow. From these infusions of color, seven continents take shape and begin to turn. Here, making becomes part of the meaning. The theatre is a place where a work can be imagined, built, activated and shared. Here, Sarkis ’ s first gesture of invitation continues into another space, where archive, memory and living bodies meet across generations. The encounter with Kantor opens a passage towards a wider encounter beyond FUGE . In different parts of Gorki, the Kantor project unfolds: an installation, two performances and a film presented during Berlin Art Week. One of Kantor ’ s earliest theatrical works, The Return of Odysseus (1944), will be revisited and reinterpreted by Mickey Mahar and Çiğdem Teke — both members of the new Gorki Ensemble — in dialogue with Bogdan Renczyński , a former member of Kantor ’ s Cricot-2 ensemble. In the early 1980s, Renczyński travelled across Kraków with Kantor, gathering materials to reconstruct the stage design of The Return of Odysseus . This reconstructed space can now be encountered in the upper foyer. From Kantor ’ s wandering stage, John Cage enters. In Litany for the Whale , two whales ’ underwater calls become music. Frank Steijns plays the work on a forty-three-bell carillon, its sound travelling through the theatre. Chandeliers made from birds’ feathers give life to the Gorki auditorium: they breathe, creating time through their breath. Movement continues in the foyer, where Sarkis ’ s Atelier de l ’ eau awaits. There, you experience the speed of colors as water, light, color and time flow through one another. Throughout FUGE , the intergenerational house-ensemble Golden Gorkis perform within this constellation, using their bodies, voices, movements and breath to carry the story of the work through the theatre. Like a fugue, histories and voices enter, disappear, return and transform one another. FUGE begins the new Gorki as a house of invitation—where art and theatre alter architecture, rhythm and how we gather. This opening expresses how we imagine us redefining the spaces of the Gorki together: not by erasing the histories they carry, but by bringing those histories into new relationships with the present—so that the theatre becomes a living organism, open throughout the day and into the night, until the last sound disappears. Sarkis turns the entire theatre into a mise-en-scène. And you are no longer sitting opposite the work. You are already inside it. FUGE continues until October 11, daily from 1pm to 9pm. Admission is free . Please join us, the new artistic team of Gorki for the opening of the 2026/27 season and the live inauguration of FUGE , on Friday, September 4, 2026, beginning at 1pm. http://www.torontotelegraph.com/news/279.text: Minister Anand meets with Hungary's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Canada News Centre 29 Sep 2026, 01:37 GMT+10 September 28, 2026 - Toronto, Ontario - Global Affairs Canada Today, the Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs, met with Anita Orban, Hungary's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the margins of the Pathways to Peace: Second International Conference on Returning Ukrainian Children, Detained Civilians, and Prisoners of War, held in Toronto on September 28 and 29, 2026. The ministers reaffirmed their strong support for Ukraine and exchanged on the importance of sustaining this support in the face of Russia's continued illegal aggression. The two ministers underscored the importance of securing the return of deported Ukrainian children, unlawfully detained civilians and prisoners of war as part of efforts to advance a just and durable peace. The ministers exchanged views on security, transatlantic cooperation and current geopolitical developments. As NATO Allies, Canada and Hungary highlighted the importance of cooperation and Minister Anand welcomed and expressed strong support for Hungary's renewed commitment to the EU and NATO. The ministers also discussed bilateral relations, including opportunities to strengthen trade and investment and people-to-people ties. Minister Anand underscored the importance of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement and encouraged Hungary to consider full ratification. The ministers exchanged on the strong historical foundations of the Canada-Hungary relationship, including the significant Hungarian-Canadian community and the enduring ties forged following Canada's resettlement of more than 37,000 Hungarian refugees after the 1956 Hungarian Revolution. The ministers highlighted the importance of continuing dialogue between Canada and Hungary and their commitment to expanding cooperation on regional security, economic prosperity and other shared international priorities.
